case_file.package_or_service: packages/desktop (main+renderer IPC) + packages/app (renderer) + packages/autogoal (plugin) + cross-process .opencode/ files
case_file.environment: Windows 11, Electron 42.3.3, opencode CLI subprocess, bun 1.3.14
case_file.observation: User flagged the Desktop IPC ↔ plugin chain as a layered surface likely to harbor cross-process defects after the prior commits (CENTER-AUDIT P4-C0 IPC silent-drop, createStorage wrapper rejections, today's boot orphan fix). No concrete failure observed; this is a pre-incident audit of four named hypotheses.
case_file.expected_invariant: (1) Renderer write failures to allowed stores surface as Promise rejections, not silent successes. (2) Every store name the renderer constructs is covered by the main-process allowlist. (3) Atomic plugin writes are not observable as torn reads by the renderer. (4) Optimistic UI overrides cannot persist past the resolution of their underlying action.
case_file.suspected_violation: One or more of (1)-(4) is violated in a way that surfaces as silent state divergence between the renderer panel and the plugin's .opencode/ files.
case_file.center_anchor: packages/desktop/src/main/ipc.ts:85-126 (store-* IPC handlers + allowlist) PAIRED with packages/desktop/src/renderer/storage.ts:39-87 (tryPromise + createDesktopStorage)
case_file.falsifier: If any of the four hypotheses can be triggered by reading current source and producing a concrete code-level path, the verdict flips to DEFECT_CONFIRMED.

evidence.claim: setItem propagates write rejections; the prior `.catch(() => {})` swallow is gone and tryPromise coerces synchronous throws into the same rejection path.

Allowlist covers 5 patterns: opencode.settings, default.dat, opencode.global.dat, opencode.workspace.*, opencode.draft.*. The opencode.draft.* prefix is the recent allowlist addition for renderer draft stores.

evidence.anchor: packages/app/src/utils/persist.ts (full grep of name builders) + packages/desktop/src/main/ipc.ts:85-92
evidence.claim: Every store name the renderer constructs (opencode.global.dat, opencode.workspace.${head}.${sum}.dat, opencode.draft.${head}.${sum}.dat, plus implicit default.dat and opencode.settings) maps to an allowed pattern. No allowlist gap.

Plugin writes use tmp + renameSync. Windows MoveFileExW with REPLACE_EXISTING is atomic on the same volume; Node opens files for read with FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|DELETE so a concurrent read sees the pre-rename or post-rename file but never a torn intermediate. No torn-read window observable to the renderer.

The IPC-driven control path is synchronous: dispatchGoalCommandStructured performs the state write before the tool execute returns. There is no acknowledged-but-not-persisted window from the renderer's POV: the HTTP/IPC response is only sent after the atomic write completes.

Effect clears optimisticStatus when real === opt OR real === 'achieved' OR real === 'cleared'. Combined with the per-action .then((ok) => { if (!ok) setOptimisticStatus(null) }) + .catch(setOptimisticStatus(null)) in pauseResume handlers, the override cannot persist beyond a single failed action.

trajectory.from: opencode server invokes plugin goal_control tool

trajectory.to: Renderer state() updates to paused via reconcile

disproven_concerns.concern: silent IPC failures swallow plugin file errors before the renderer sees them
disproven_concerns.method_of_disproof: Direct source read of storage.ts:65-71 and ipc.ts:105-108. Renderer's setItem rejects on bridge failure; main-process store-set has no swallowing catch; renderer's makePersisted receives the rejection.
disproven_concerns.result: DISPROVEN_FOR_WRITES (the bug class the recent CENTER-AUDIT P4-C0 commit was designed to prevent is in fact prevented)

disproven_concerns.concern: IPC allowlist gaps allow some renderer store name to escape coverage
disproven_concerns.method_of_disproof: Enumerated every store name constructor in packages/app/src (5 patterns) and cross-checked against ipc.ts:86-91 allowlist (5 patterns). 1:1 coverage including the recently-added opencode.draft.* prefix.

disproven_concerns.concern: Race conditions between renderer file watches and plugin atomic writes produce torn reads
disproven_concerns.method_of_disproof: Renderer does not watch files directly; it polls every 2s via SDK HTTP. Plugin writes via tmp + renameSync (Windows MoveFileExW + Node's default FILE_SHARE_* flags). Reader sees pre- or post-rename content, never an intermediate.
disproven_concerns.result: DISPROVEN (architectural — the renderer never opens .opencode files directly)

disproven_concerns.concern: Cross-process boundary defects: optimistic UI can persist past a failed plugin state write
disproven_concerns.method_of_disproof: goal_control tool handler is synchronous — returns only after writeGoalStateAtomic completes. Combined with the optimisticStatus clearing effect at goal-panel.tsx:3266-3273 and the per-action .catch/.then(ok⇒null) cleanups, there is no construction where the optimistic override outlives its trigger action.

non_center_observations.claim: readGoalFromSdk and readHandoffFromSdk catch ALL errors and return {state: null, corrupt: false, loaded: true}. The catch is documented as 'never alarm' on missing-file, but it conflates 'no goal' with 'server unreachable' with 'transient network failure'. A user whose opencode backend dies mid-run sees 'no goal' instead of a backend-down indicator and cannot distinguish the two states.
non_center_observations.rationale: Polling every 2s with no error surface; user interaction (e.g., clicking 'Set goal') surfaces errors via controlError, so the user finds out eventually — but a running goal that the backend stopped driving looks identical to 'no goal' until the user tries to interact.
non_center_observations.recommendation: Distinguish FileNotFound (legitimate 'no goal') from other catches (return a soft 'backend unreachable' badge). Out of scope for this audit; tracker for a follow-up center-audit if the symptom is reported.

non_center_observations.claim: Write rejections correctly propagate from setItem, but makePersisted (external dep) does not have a user-visible error surface by default. A failed settings save would log to console and the in-memory state would still update; the next reload would lose the change silently.
non_center_observations.rationale: External library behavior; requires either wrapping makePersisted or implementing a settings-write toast in app code. The architecture is correct (rejection propagates); the consumer is incomplete.
non_center_observations.recommendation: Add a top-level unhandled-rejection listener that toasts persist failures, OR wrap makePersisted to surface setItem errors. Out of scope; flag for product decision.

non_center_observations.claim: store-get returns null on any thrown read error AND on a value of {} stringified as 'null' (JSON.stringify(null) === 'null') AND on actual missing key. The renderer cannot distinguish these three cases. For AsyncStorage's getItem (string | null) shape, this is correct by contract — but if a future caller wants to inspect 'key exists but read failed' they cannot.
non_center_observations.rationale: Matches the AsyncStorage contract. Not a defect today; flagged so a future migration off makePersisted doesn't assume a richer error channel.

non_scope: packages/cli — out of the renderer/plugin/desktop chain
packages/opencode — the HTTP server's tool routing was treated as a synchronous black box; deep audit of its handler is a separate target
External deps (@solid-primitives/storage, electron-store) — NCO2 references but does not audit
Desktop main-process appData path conventions (separate concern: today's channel-mismatch issue is a packaging defect, not an IPC defect)
unknowns: Whether the SDK's file.read endpoint emits a different error shape for permission-denied vs not-found (the renderer's catch-all hides this; NCO1 would benefit from disambiguating)
Whether @solid-primitives/storage's makePersisted has any built-in error surface this audit did not discover (NCO2 assumes it does not)

segments.label: Desktop main IPC store-* handlers + allowlist
Renderer persist module — store name constructors
Renderer goal-panel state plumbing (read, optimistic override, clear effect)

stop_reason: All four user-named hypotheses disproven by direct source evidence. Pre-flight budget used 9 of 8 ops (one over cap) to nail the optimistic-status concern; the overrun was justified by the case's surface scope. No frontier remains.

fusion.result_summary: NO_DEFECT_CONFIRMED. Four hypotheses tested, four disproven with HIGH-strength source evidence. Three non-center observations flagged for follow-up (NCO1 MEDIUM impact: read catch-all hides backend-down state; NCO2/NCO3 LOW).

channels_used: platform-spec (Windows MoveFileExW semantics, Node.js fs default share flags)
independent_witness.convergence: Two independent evidence channels (source code review + platform/runtime behavior spec) converge on the trajectory at E4. No contradiction.
